message.content:
On the remote coast of Nova Scotia, where the sea roared like a beast and the wind howled like a ghost, lived an old lighthouse keeper named Elias. He had tended the light for over thirty years, his days marked by the rhythm of the waves and the flicker of the beacon. The lighthouse stood alone, a sentinel against the storm, and Elias had long since grown used to the silence.

One stormy evening, as the sea churned and the sky turned the color of bruised fruit, Elias was cleaning the lens when he noticed something unusual. A bottle, half-buried in the sand near the base of the tower, caught his eye. Curious, he dug it out, his hands trembling with age and the cold.

Inside the bottle was a single sheet of paper, the ink faded but legible. The message was written in a hurried hand: *"I am lost at sea. My ship was wrecked, and I am the only survivor. If you can read this, please help me. I am near the island of St. Pierre. I have no food, no water, and no hope."*

Elias’s heart sank. He had heard stories of the island, a place where the sea was treacherous
